<reason>PRO won the central clash: a static unit price does not alert habitual shoppers that the deal changed, while a time-limited change flag does. PRO also gave a workable regular-price, 60-90 day rule and answered the implementation challenge with the symmetry that if retailers link a replacement to sell it, they can link it to disclose the drop. CON's comparator and retailer-burden concerns remained serious, but its clearer-current-price alternative did not explain how shoppers notice change, and its deterrence objection was turned into evidence of restored transparency.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Most decisive was PRO turning CON's claim that brands would simply raise headline prices into a concession: visible headline increases are noticed and need no badge, proving flags push competition from stealth shrinkage into transparent pricing.</best_rebuttal>
